record.context_brief: Classification of rational maps with Herman rings
record.original_question: Which rational maps, especially in low degrees such as 3 and 4, admit Herman rings? More specifically, can one give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a Herman ring in terms of the map's degree, the configuration of critical orbits, and combinatorial data, and can one describe the associated parameter slices using tools such as Teichmuller theory and quasiconformal deformation theory?

evidence.quote: It is known that rational functions of degree 2 cannot have any Herman rings. However, further investigation is needed to classify all rational functions that can admit Herman rings, particularly in low degrees (degree 3 or 4), where examples are still limited. Despite several known constructions, a complete characterization of rational maps admitting Herman rings is still lacking. In particular, it remains open to identify necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of degree, critical orbit configurations, and combinatorial data. It is also fascinating to investigate parameter slices for families of functions with a Herman ring. Using Teichmuller theory and quasiconformal deformation theory to map out these regions can also be explored.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Herman ring of a rational map $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ is a periodic Fatou component $U$ that is conformally isomorphic to a round annulus $A_r=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:1<|z|<r\}$ for some $r>1$, on which (for some period $p\geq 1$) the iterate $f^{\circ p}$ is conjugate, via this isomorphism, to an irrational rigid rotation $z\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$ of $A_r$. By a theorem of Shishikura, every rational map possessing a Herman ring has degree at least $3$.

Provide a complete classification of rational maps $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ that admit a Herman ring, with emphasis on low degrees (in particular degrees $3$ and $4$). More precisely, accomplish the following:

(a) Give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a Herman ring of $f$ purely in terms of:
   (i) the degree $d=\deg(f)$,
   (ii) the configuration of the critical orbits of $f$ (the forward orbits of the critical points, including their mutual interactions and accumulation behavior), and
   (iii) combinatorial data describing how the Julia set and the Fatou components of $f$ are arranged (such as a suitable invariant graph, lamination, or puzzle-piece structure encoding the dynamics).

(b) For natural one- or several-parameter families of rational maps containing maps with Herman rings, describe the corresponding parameter slices — i.e. the loci of parameters for which a Herman ring of given combinatorics persists — using Teichmüller theory and quasiconformal deformation theory, and determine the topology, conformal structure, and boundary behavior of these loci.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of rational maps admitting Herman rings, especially in degrees 3 and 4, is widely recognized as open. Shishikura proved degree ≥ 3 is necessary, and explicit constructions exist (e.g., cubic rational maps with smooth degenerate Herman rings, due to Yang and collaborators), but no necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of degree, critical orbit configurations, and combinatorial data are known, and the structure of associated parameter slices remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Rational maps with smooth degenerate Herman rings
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of cubic rational maps with smooth degenerate Herman rings, indicating ongoing investigation into low-degree examples.
status_evidence.claim: Examples of degree-3 rational maps with (degenerate) Herman rings have been constructed, but a full classification is not given.

status_evidence.title: Herman ring - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Shishikura showed that if a rational function possesses a Herman ring, then the degree of the function is at least 3.
status_evidence.claim: The minimum degree for a Herman ring is 3 (Shishikura), but no complete characterization is given.

status_evidence.title: Rational maps with smooth degenerate Herman rings - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work constructing new examples rather than classifying all such maps.
status_evidence.claim: Research is producing new constructions, supporting that the classification problem remains open.
